LESSON: SIGN READING 11.2.1 INTENSIVE SIGN READING SIGN READING WITH TECHNOLOGY

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.2: Sign Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading Sign Reading with Technology
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading Sign Reading with Technology, part of Strand 11 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five General.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to relate what you read to real life experiences? 2. What digital resources can you use in your reading?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading Sign Reading with Technology together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
•Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: Research skills as learners search and sign read texts from the internet.

•Communication and collaboration: Articulating signs clearly: as learners observe fingerspell and sign words related to the theme; sports.

•Creativity and imagination: Making connections as learners, in groups or pairs, create pictures, mimes, videos or crossword puzzles.

Values:
• Responsibility: Determination as learners dramatise or role play events or characters in stories they have read and sign read online.

• Love: Sharing as learners display in a gallery walk visuals obtained from online sources.

Link to other Subjects:

Learners are able to relate the skill of intensive sign reading to their learning in all learning areas.
